refuted.claim: Arithmetic overflow is an indicator of Zero and Add, Zero and Subtract, Multiply and (implicitly) Divide. The Part-A instruction table lists 'zero balance; arith overflow' under Indicators for the `?` (ZA), `!` (ZS) and `@` (M) rows, and the 'Indicators set/reset by Part-A operations' table says arithmetic overflow is 'Set by Add, Subtract (and any op where the result exceeds the B-field word-mark limit)'.
refuted.why: The IBM 1410 Principles of Operation states the opposite explicitly, in identical wording in editions 2 and 3: 'This light shows that an arithmetic-overflow condition has been detected. The overflow condition can be detected only during an add or subtract operation, and not during a zero and add, zero and subtract, multiply or divide operation.' The finder's own fact #8 quotes the overflow rule from p.16, which sits inside the Add/Subtract discussion; the generalisation to every op whose result exceeds the B-field word mark is the error. This is emulator-behaviour-changing: a 1410 emulator that raises arithmetic overflow on a ZA/ZS/multiply whose A field is longer than the B field will diverge from the machine, and a program that does ZA followed by BAV will branch when it should not.
refuted.correction: Only Add and Subtract (one-field or two-field form) can set the arithmetic-overflow indicator. Zero and Add, Zero and Subtract and Multiply never set it, even when high-order A-field digits are cut off by the B-field word mark. Divide never sets arithmetic overflow either; it sets the separate divide-overflow indicator (quotient field two or more positions short, or division by zero). The Part-A table's Indicators column for `?`, `!`, `@` should read 'zero balance' only, and `%` should read 'divide overflow' only.
refuted.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3, printed p.53 ('Overflow' console-light description, 1415 Console section) - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt ; identical text in A22-0526-2 (archive item bitsavers_ibm1410A22_13458542, same section). PDFs: http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf

refuted.claim: Divide (% aaaaa bbbbb): 'B-address = LEFTMOST position of the dividend (i.e. of the quotient-dividend field)'.
refuted.why: The parenthetical equates the leftmost position of the dividend with the leftmost position of the quotient/dividend field. The manual says they are different positions: 'The A-address specifies the units position of the divisor. The B-address specifies the leftmost position of the dividend. The dividend itself is located in the rightmost positions of the quotient-dividend (B) field.' Figure 17 makes it concrete: divisor 12 (2 digits), dividend 14700 (5 digits) gives a B field of 8 positions holding 00014700; the three leading zeros are the quotient area and the B-address is the '1' of 14700, i.e. position 4 of 8, not position 1. Note 1 on p.21 stresses the point: 'it is important to address the leftmost position of the dividend (B-address of the divide instruction). This ensures that the first divide operation results in a single high-order quotient digit. An improperly addressed dividend can cause a divide overflow condition if the result of the first divide operation is greater than 9.' An emulator that starts divide at the left end of the whole B field will produce wrong quotients and spurious divide overflows. (The finder's own table row states it correctly - 'B = LEFTMOST position of the dividend inside the quotient/dividend field' - so only the facts-list parenthetical is wrong.)
refuted.correction: The B-address of Divide is the leftmost position of the DIVIDEND, which sits (divisor length + 1) positions in from the left end of the quotient/dividend field. The quotient develops leftward from there; its units position ends up at (address of the units position of the dividend) - (length of divisor) - 1. Cross-checked against SimH i7010_cpu.c do_divide(), which sets DAR = BAR and walks DAR rightward one position per quotient digit, complement-adding leftward from each window.
refuted.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3, printed pp.20-21 ('Divide', items 1-3 and Notes 1-4, Figures 15-17) - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt ; same text in A22-0526-2 p.20. Emulator cross-check: https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_cpu.c (do_divide)

refuted.claim: Open question: 'Edition A22-0526-3 (the last edition) was not readable without OCR - image-only, and no OCR mirror found. Should be spot-checked against edition 2 before freezing tables.' All PoO citations in the findings therefore rest on the edition-2 OCR only.
refuted.why: An Internet Archive OCR of edition 3 exists and is complete: item bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698, file A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt. I read the whole instruction-description section of edition 3 for this verification.
refuted.correction: Edition 3 IS machine-readable via the Internet Archive OCR. I spot-checked ~25 instruction descriptions in edition 3 against the finder's tables (instruction formats and valid lengths p.11, chaining and op-modifier blanking p.12, Figure 7 timing symbols p.12, Figure 8 register symbols p.13, indexing-overflow note p.15, sign/add-cycle/digit-coding Figures 11-13 p.16-18, Add/Subtract/ZA/ZS one- and two-field forms pp.17-19, Multiply p.19-20, Divide pp.20-21, SAR p.22, SW/CW p.22, Clear Storage and Clear Storage and Branch p.23, Halt/Halt and Branch p.23, NOP p.24, Move d-character Figures 19-22 pp.25-27, MCS pp.27-28, Compare p.28, Table Lookup and Figure 25 pp.29-30, MCE and Figures 28-31 pp.31-33, Figure 35 branch d-characters p.36) and found NO substantive difference from the edition-2 text on any of them, including every timing formula and register result. The tables can be frozen. The one edition-2-vs-3 spot-check I could run mechanically (Add/Subtract timing, SAR T=69.75, the divide B-address sentence) is byte-identical in wording.

upgraded.claim: Set Word Mark op code is the comma (BCD A821). Previously sourced partly to SimH's CHR_COM=033 and to the OCR-lossy PoO appendix, where the op-code glyph did not survive scanning.
upgraded.source: Two independent PRIMARY text-layer sources: IBM 1410 CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.16 op-code-lengths chart, row ', (A)(B)  Set Word Mark  6  11*' - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf ; and CE Instruction-Reference 223-2589 (System Fundamentals, Nov 63) op-code chart, row ',(A)(B) Set Word Mark  1  6  11' - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf . The CE Handbook 'Miscellaneous Oper' table (p.25) also spells out all three forms: ',(A)(B)', ',(A)', ',(no address)'.

upgraded.claim: Clear Word Mark op code is the lozenge (BCD BA84, card 12-8-4). Previously leaned on SimH OP_CWM = CHR_LPARN = 074.
upgraded.source: PRIMARY: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3 alphabetic instruction appendix, row 'Clear Word Mark (Two Addresses)  CW a,b  [lozenge](A)(B)' (printed p.22 reference) - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt ; and CE Instruction-Reference 223-2589 op-code chart row '[lozenge](A)(B)  Clear Word Mark  1  6  11'.

upgraded.claim: The d-character for SCNLA (BCD 16, A bit only) is the 'substitute blank' character - the finder listed this as an unresolved glyph in open_questions.
upgraded.source: PRIMARY: A22-0526-3 Figure 2 special-character legend lists 'Substitute Blank' as a distinct 1410 graphic (rendered as a struck b) alongside 'Blank'; the Figure 22 move matrix and the appendix row 'Scan Left thru 1st A-Field wm  SCNLA a,b  D (A)(B) [substitute blank]' both carry that glyph in the A-bit-only cell - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt . Corroborated by SimH I7000/i7000_defs.h '#define CHR_BLANK 020' (A bit only) as distinct from '#define CHR_ABLANK 000'.

additions.claim: Divide: the DIVISOR may be unsigned. 'If no bits are in the units position of the divisor, the system assumes that the divisor is positive.' Only the dividend is required to carry a sign (B+A for plus, B for minus), and it is that sign that stops the division. The dividend is destroyed during the operation except for the remainder.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3 p.20, 'Divide' item 3 'Sign and Zeros' - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt

additions.claim: Divide: an improperly addressed dividend (B-address not at its leftmost position) can itself cause a divide overflow, because the first divide step then yields a result greater than 9. Separately, if a larger quotient is wanted, zeros are appended to the RIGHT of the dividend - one zero per extra quotient digit (Figure 17). Both are emulator-visible consequences of the same field layout.
additions.source: A22-0526-3 p.21, Divide Notes 1 and 4, Figure 17 - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt

additions.claim: Table Lookup uses the C-address register to restart each argument comparison: 'At the start of each search cycle, the C-address register automatically receives this address [the A-address, the rightmost position of the search argument] and, if no hit is made, replaces it in the A-address register so the search can be repeated at the next table argument to the left.' An emulator must reload AAR from a saved copy at the start of every table-field comparison, not just decrement it.

The 1410 Accelerator does not merely substitute timing formulas: it reduces the core-storage cycle from 4.5 to 4.0 microseconds and shortens the cycle length of data operations, for an internal speed-up of about 23% and a 15-23% throughput gain. Worked examples: Add (one field) T = 4(L+1+2A), L=1 or 6; Add (two fields) T = 4(L+1+E+A+B+RB) with E=1 when L=1, E=0 when L=11; one-address conditional branch T = 4(L+1+C), L=1 or 7; Branch if Bit/Character Equal T = 4(L+2.5+C), L=1, 6 or 12. 'The accelerated system is otherwise identical to the unchanged system.'

Compare: when the A-field is shorter than the B-field, the A-field MUST have a word mark (otherwise the operation has no stopping condition on that side); that case turns on the high indicator. The finder recorded the high-indicator effect but not the word-mark requirement.
additions.source: IBM 1410 CE Handbook 223-2588-2, 'Brief Op Code Descriptions', Comparing row, Word Marks column: 'Operation is terminated by either an A-fd or B-fd word mark. If A-fd is shorter than B-fd, A-fd must have WM. In this case Hi-ind is on.' - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf

additions.claim: The 'last instruction in the program needs a word mark immediately to its right' rule applies to Halt and Branch as well as to plain Halt: 'Word Marks: Word marks are not affected. If this is the last instruction in the program, a word mark must be preset in the storage location immediately to the right of the halt and branch instruction.'

Move Characters and Edit truncation rule the finder omitted: 'The edited output field does not contain any A-field data that have not been moved before the word mark for the control field is sensed.' i.e. the B-field (control-field) word mark hard-stops the forward scan and any remaining A data is simply dropped.
additions.source: A22-0526-3 p.31, 'Move Characters and Edit', Word Marks - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt

additions.claim: The CE Instruction-Reference 223-2589 op-code chart gives a THREE-column acceptable-length table that includes the 1-character chained form the CE Handbook chart omits: A/S/?/!/@/% = 1,6,11; B/W/V (branch if char/bit equal, branch on WM/zone) = 1,6,12; D (move) = 1,6,12; Z (MCS) = 1,6,11; E (MCE) = 1,6,11; C (compare) = 1,6,11; T (table lookup) = 1,6,12; G (SAR) = 7; ',' (SW) = 1,6,11; lozenge (CW) = 1,6,11; '/' (clear storage and branch) = 1,6,11; '.' (halt and branch) = 1,6; J = 1,7; R/X = 7; N = no length; M/L = 10; U = 5. This resolves the finder's uncertainty about whether the 1-character chained form is universally legal - it is, for every processing op.
additions.source: IBM 1410 CE Instruction Reference: System Fundamentals, 223-2589 (Nov 1963), op-code table - http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/223-2589_Instruction_Reference_1410_System_Fundamentals_Nov63.pdf

additions.claim: The 1410 floating-point feature does NOT overload any Part-A op-code character: SimH's 7010 defines OP_FP as CHR_EQ (the '=' character, BCD 8-2-1, octal 013), which is unused by every op in the Part-A set. This closes one of the finder's open questions for the SimH-defined feature set (it does not by itself prove the 1401-compatibility feature is clean).

Add/Subtract data-validity behaviour the finder omitted: 'The BCD characters to be added are checked for valid BCD coding, and an invalid bit combination causes an A or B channel error. The characters are then translated to qui-binary code and fed to the adder. The adder's output is retranslated to BCD; an invalid combination of bits at this point causes an assembly channel error.' A faithful emulator should model these as machine checks, not silently accept the character.

Zero-balance indicator reset detail: besides the next non-zero-result arithmetic op, the indicator is also cleared by a power-on reset as well as by computer reset. The console-light text enumerates the setting ops as 'any add, subtract, zero and add, zero and subtract, or multiply operation' - divide is absent from both the set and the reset list, matching the p.16 rule.

Support for the finder's 'likely' Move-Characters-and-Suppress-Zeros direction claim, from a primary source but by inference rather than by statement: the PoO's own register result for MCS is AAR = A - LA. A DECREASING A-address register is only consistent with the A-address being the field's rightmost (units) position and the copy pass running right-to-left; a left-to-right copy would leave A + LA, as it does for every left-to-right Move (Figure 20). The manual never says this in words in any edition.
additions.source: A22-0526-3 p.27 (MCS 'Address Registers after Operation') compared with Figure 20 p.26 - https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt ; behavioural confirmation only in SimH i7010_cpu.c case OP_MSZ (DownReg(AAR)/DownReg(BAR) copy pass, then UpReg(BAR) forward suppression pass)

notes:
Method: I did not re-download anything. The session scratchpad already held full Internet Archive OCR text for BOTH A22-0526-2 (poo2.txt) and A22-0526-3 (po_ocr.txt, 27601 lines, header 'Form A22-0526-3'), plus text-layer extractions of CE Handbook 223-2588-2 (ceh.txt), CE Instruction-Reference 223-2589 (instref.txt), the Nov-61 reference manual A22-1407-2 (ref1407.txt), and local copies of SimH rcornwell/sims I7000/i7010_cpu.c, i7010_defs.h, i7000_defs.h. Everything below was read in edition 3 unless noted.

Spot-checked rows (23, against the manual's own instruction descriptions - format, lengths, word marks, terminator, register results, timing): Add two-field, Add one-field, Subtract two-field, Subtract one-field, Zero and Add two-field, Zero and Add one-field, Zero and Subtract two-field (incl. Figure 13 sign map), Zero and Subtract one-field, Multiply, Divide, Compare, Table Lookup (incl. Figure 25 d-modifiers 1-7 and blank), Move/Scan (incl. Figure 19 bit encoding, Figure 20 register results, Figure 21 mnemonic construction, Figure 22 full 64-cell matrix), Move Characters and Suppress Zeros, Move Characters and Edit (incl. Figure 28 control characters, zero suppression, asterisk protection, floating dollar, sign control left, decimal control), Store Address Register, Set Word Mark, Clear Word Mark, Clear Storage, Clear Storage and Branch, Halt, Halt and Branch, No Operation. Also verified: instruction formats and valid lengths (1/2/5/6/7/10/11/12) p.11, chaining plus the op-modifier-blanking rule for the 11-position form p.12, Figure 7 timing symbols, Figure 8 register symbols, indexing-does-not-set-overflow p.15, Figure 11 sign bits, Figure 12 add-cycle selection, digit coding p.16, Figure 35 branch d-characters (Z/S/U/T//-slash/W/V), and the computer-reset indicator behaviour p.36.

Everything in the finder's tables held up EXCEPT the two items in `refuted` (arithmetic overflow attributed to ZA/ZS/Multiply; the divide B-address parenthetical). The 64-cell move matrix, the mnemonic construction rules (L = right-to-left, R = left-to-right - counter-intuitive but correct), the d-character terminator encoding, the Table Lookup d-modifier values, and all SimH BCD op-code constants (A=061, S=022, ?=072, !=052, @=014, %=034, G=067, ','=033, lozenge=074, '/'=021, '.'=073, N=045, D=064, Z=031, C=063, T=023, E=065) are correct.

1401-vs-1410 confusion hunt: I found NONE. The three highest-risk items all check out as genuine 1410 facts, and in each case the 1410 differs from the 1401 in exactly the way the finder recorded. (a) Compare terminates on EITHER an A- or a B-field word mark and a short A field sets HIGH - this is the 1410 rule, verified verbatim at p.28, and is not the 1401 rule. (b) There is no Load op; L and M are the 1410's Read/Write-with/without-word-marks I/O op codes, confirmed in the PoO appendix ('M or L' appears in every card/tape/printer row) and in both CE op-code charts. (c) Data movement really is unified into the single op D with a 6-bit d-character; the 1401's separate move/load ops do not exist. The finder's negative results (no Load, no Move-and-Insert-Zeros, no Translate/Convert in the base set) survive an independent pass over the ed-3 alphabetic instruction appendix and both CE op-code charts.

Could not upgrade: the Move-Characters-and-Suppress-Zeros scan direction. No edition of the PoO, the Nov-61 reference manual A22-1407-2 (identical wording), or the CE Handbook states it. The strongest primary evidence is the AAR = A - LA register result, which forces the reading (see additions). It remains 'likely'. The interruptibility semantics behind the CE Handbook's asterisks, and whether the 1401-compatibility feature (223-2597) overloads a Part-A op character, were out of scope and remain open - I checked only the SimH floating-point op character.

Sourcing note for downstream use: prefer the edition-3 archive OCR (https://archive.org/download/bitsavers_ibm1410A22_14511698/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps_djvu.txt) over the edition-2 mirror the findings cite. Same content on every point checked, and it is the last edition. Page numbers throughout are the manual's printed page numbers, taken from running footers; PDF page offsets were not established (the finder's caveat stands).
